text:
oliver: Quick triage — upstream released patches for CVE-2026-1045 (libssl) and CVE-2026-2042 (glibc dlopen overflow). Affects ubuntu:22.04-based and alpine:3.18-based images we ship. Need rebuild plan + QA. Priority: high. :exclamation:
sara: Which services use the ubuntu/alpine variants? runtime, dedicated GPU pools, private helm charts?
ben: Runtime + dedicated + private images. Also CI images for model build. Full matrix: x86_64 and arm64, ubuntu(glibc) and alpine(musl).
lina: Agree on matrix. Suggestations: quick canary on staging, then 2% production traffic, then full rollout. We should run TLS handshake smoke + our internal TLS mutual auth tests.
mike: Ops question — do we need a KMS key rotation / re-sign images as part of this? Signing currently gated by infra-signer role. If we rebuild, we should sign and attach attestations. RBAC: infra-signer must be the only role allowed to promote.
sec-bot: [automated] CVE-2026-1045 link: https://nvd.example/CVE-2026-1045 - patch available in openssl 3.1.10; CVE-2026-2042 fixed in glibc 2.38.
ben: For alpine, openssl is in apk, but musl-based images may behave differently. Need to test libssl ABI compatibility for our binary wheels.
oliver: Test plan draft:
- rebuild base images with patched packages
- run container unit smoke: startup, healthcheck, TLS handshake to our test certs
- run integration: grpc call/stream tests, high-concurrency request pattern for 10m
- run memory/ASAN regression on arm64 where possible
- signing + promote to canary cluster
- monitor TLS error rate, core dumps, increase canary to 2% after 2 hours if clean
(keeping it short so SRE can automate)
sara: Add audit logging check: ensure image promotion events are recorded to audit-log with subject, key-id, and build SHA. retention policy should capture this for 90 days for compliance.
mike: Will add an enforceable RBAC policy change: only "infra-signer" and "release-oncall" can call promote-image. I will open a PR and schedule a 30m review with p0 approvers.
lina: CI snippets — build commands we should run in parallel (x86/arm):
```
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t registry.redwood/base:patched-2026-04 --push .
# or separate per-arch with qemu if needed
```
ben: Also capture package manager pins for reproducibility: apt pin + apk manifest snapshot. Store them in the image metadata file and in the SBOM.
sec-bot: [automated] Reminder: update SBOM and attach to image attestation. CVE-2026-1045 and CVE-2026-2042 must be listed in the remediation ticket metadata.
oliver: Timeline proposal: start builds in next 6 hours, run canary in staging tonight, production canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC, full rollout by EOD tomorrow if no regressions. Is that realistic?
sara: Sounds tight but OK if we parallelize. Priority: block non-compliant images from being deployed by enforcement policy (image policy deny list) until patched images promoted. Can security ops flip the deny flag?
mike: Yes. Will add temporary admission controller rule to deny old tags matching our vulnerable digest patterns. Need list of digests — infra team will produce.
ben: Tests to watch during canary: TLS handshake failures, openssl errors in logs, segfaults, and perf regressions >5% P95 latency. Capture traces.
lina: Also verify multiarch manifest resolves correctly on GKE and ecs-fargate for arm64. We saw a manifest selector bug last quarter.
sec-bot: [automated] Suggested labels for the remediation ticket: [P1][base-image][openssl][glibc][multiarch][signed].
oliver: Owners: oliver (security lead) to coordinate, ben (infra) to run builds, lina (runtime) to run canaries and tests, mike (ops) to update RBAC + admission, sara (compliance) to own audit retention. I'll create the JIRA and include this thread.
sara: Final quick note — remember to validate KMS access logs show only authorized signing events; if we see unfamiliar principals, pause promotion.
oliver: OK locking this in. Action items in JIRA by EOD. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
